glyph_origin: In oracle bone script, ideogrammic compound (會意): 幺 (“thread”) + 夊 (“foot”) – a foot bound by a rope, thus lagging behind. The component 彳 was added afterwards to emphasize this action. Note that the simplified form 后 is also a traditional character on its own, with a different meaning.
s_page_origin: Multiple theories exist regarding its primary sense: • One traditional view (e.g., Shuowen) interprets it as a reversed form of 司 (“to manage; to command”), depicting a person issuing decrees from within (symbolized by 口 (“mouth”)), with the original meaning of "sovereign; ruler" (such as the Xia dynasty rulers). However, this view is considered questionable in contemporary paleography. • Another theory (e.g., Wang Guowei) posits a phonetic and semantic connection with 毓 (“to give birth”). Wang argued that the sense of "monarch" extended from the notion of 繼嗣 ("continuing the lineage"). Crucially, while the character 毓 graphically depicts a woman giving birth (a head-down delivery), the oracle bone form of 后 does not share this visual depiction; this connection is just phonological and etymological, rather than a direct graphic evolution. • Recent epigraphic studies suggest that oracle bone forms of 后 and 司 were largely interchangeable, often functioning as 司 in sacrificial contexts rather than representing 后. See also the ongoing debate regarding 后母戊鼎.
note: Composite id: 后 also writes other words; this sign is the 後 sense. glyph_origin is from the 後 page; s_page_origin is the 后 page's own text.
